You and a friend play a game: you each pick a sequence of 3 coin-flip outcomes in advance (like HHT), then flip a fair coin repeatedly until one of your sequences appears first in the stream — that person wins. Your friend picks HHH. You get to choose your sequence AFTER seeing theirs. Which sequence should you pick, and what is your probability of winning with it?
choices: HHT, with a 50% chance of winning
TTT, with a 50% chance of winning
THH, with a 7/8 chance of winning
HTH, with a 1/2 chance of winning

questions.q: Assume 12 equally likely birth months (ignore leap years). How many people must be in a room before the probability that at least two of them share the same birth month exceeds 50%?

Die A has faces {2,2,4,4,9,9}. Die B has faces {1,1,6,6,8,8}. Die C has faces {3,3,5,5,7,7}. Each die is rolled against each other die many times (higher face wins each roll). Which statement is true?
choices: All three dice win against each other equally often, with no advantage either way
Die A beats Die B, Die B beats Die C, and Die C beats Die A — there's no single 'best' die
Die A beats both B and C, since it has the highest face value (9)
Die C beats both A and B, since its faces are the most balanced

A hotel has infinitely many rooms, numbered 1, 2, 3, ..., and every single room is already occupied by a guest. One more guest arrives asking for a room. Can the hotel accommodate them without evicting anyone?
choices: No — every room is full, so there is no room for another guest
No — infinity plus one is undefined, so the question has no answer
Yes, but only if the hotel first builds an extra room
Yes — move the guest in room n to room n+1 for every n, freeing up room 1
